subject: Can't run STAN even though compilation works ok and c++ compiler seems to be present

messages.author: 3d8288d2d8fd30fb
messages.subject: Can't run STAN even though compilation works ok and c++ compiler seems to be present
parts:
Running Windows 7, downloaded latest version of rstan/stan, rtools, inline.  The attached log lists the verbose result of running the programs described in the user documentation.  C++ compiler seems to be present and operating.  The PATH setting seems to be right.  I tried using the schools example, to reproduce the example in the manual.  Compilation via 'stanc' seems to have worked ok.  However, I get errors when I try to execute stan_model with the output from stanc.  The sequence of steps is the same as on p. 6 of the R interface to Stan.   

In the attached log, my entries are in red, and I have highlighted where the errors occur in light green.

I'm not a C expert, so have no idea how to interpret the output.  Any ideas as to what is wrong?

Thanks for your help.

Larry Gould

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can't run STAN even though compilation works ok and c++ compiler seems to be present
parts:
Hi Larry,

Can you try setting Stan to fast mode? Replace set_cppo(mode="debug") to set_cppo(mode="fast").

I think in Windows, using the 32 bit g++ distributed by RTools, we are hitting the memory limit.



Daniel
